en.headline: Two flats burgled at Ngau Chi Wan estate during major renovation
en.dek: Police are treating the cases at Hilltop Gardens as a serial burglary after gold jewellery worth about HK$320,000 was taken from two units in the same block.
body: Police said two residential flats in Block 2 of Hilltop Gardens on Fung Shing Street in Ngau Chi Wan were burgled within hours of each other while the estate undergoes major renovation works with scaffolding covering the exterior.

In the first case on Wednesday evening, a 64-year-old woman reported that a window had been prised open and gold jewellery worth about HK$80,000 was missing. On Thursday morning, a 50-year-old woman in another flat on the same block found a window forced and reported the loss of gold and jewellery valued at about HK$240,000.

Officers believe the intruders entered via the windows, possibly using the scaffolding. The cases have been merged into a single serial burglary investigation by the Wong Tai Sin district crime squad. No arrests have been made.
The management office has written to owners reminding them to secure windows and report suspicious persons, noting that contractor staff are frequently entering the estate during the works.

zh.headline: 牛池灣海港花園大維修期間兩單位遭連環爆竊失約32萬金器
zh.dek: 警方將案件合併列作連環爆竊調查，同座兩個單位窗戶被撬，共失約32萬元金器珠寶，暫未有人被捕。
body: 警方表示，牛池灣豐盛街海港花園第二座兩個住宅單位在短時間內接連被爆竊，當時屋苑正進行大型維修，外牆搭有棚架。
首宗案件於周三晚上發生，64歲女住戶報稱窗戶被撬開，失去約8萬元金器。周四早上，同座另一單位50歲女住戶發現窗戶被撬及屋內被搜掠，初步點算失去約24萬元金器及珠寶。
警方相信賊人從窗戶進入，可能利用棚架，已將兩宗案件合併為連環爆竊，由黃大仙警區刑事調查隊跟進，目前未有人被捕。
管理處已向業戶發信，提醒檢查門窗並注意可疑人士，指維修期間承建商人員會頻繁進出屋苑。
